steps.title: Как это работает
steps.html:
Правила, выводимого из смысла, здесь нет. Модель принадлежит первому глаголу, и её учат вместе с глаголом — как предлог.

Полезная опора: глаголы про нравится и продолжается тяготеют к -ing; про решение и план — к to.

После любого предлога всегда -ing: interested in learning, instead of going, good at explaining.

Stop меняет смысл: He stopped smoking — бросил. He stopped to smoke — остановился, чтобы покурить.

steps.title: Before you read: some films are watched all over the world, and others never leave the country that made them.
steps.sub: What do you think matters most?

steps.title: A film that travels
steps.html:
Some films cross borders effortlessly. Others, made with far more money, stop at the first subtitle. What is the difference?

A  In 2019, a South Korean film about a poor family and a rich one won the biggest prize in world cinema. Its director had a warning for audiences who avoid foreign films: once you get over the one-inch barrier of subtitles, he said, you will find many more films worth watching. The remark stuck, because it named something the industry has always known. Most films never leave home, and the reason is rarely the quality of the plot.

B  Nigeria produces more films than almost anywhere on earth. The industry there tends to work fast and cheaply, and it has an audience that stretches far beyond Nigeria: its fans log in from Brazil, India and the United States. Producers have learned to showcase African culture to the world rather than to imitate Hollywood, and audiences seem to enjoy watching stories they have not already seen a hundred times. A growing middle class looking for entertainment has done the rest.

C  So what travels? Not, it turns out, special effects. Distributors who study this say the films that cross borders most easily are built on a situation any audience recognises immediately: a family under pressure, a person who decides to set out on a journey, somebody who wants to escape a life that has closed around them. The cast can be unknown and the budget small. What matters is that a viewer in another country does not need to be told why the character is doing this.

D  Genre helps too, but not in the way people expect. Animated films travel well because the voices can be replaced. Thrillers travel because tension needs very few words. Comedy travels worst of all: a joke often depends on the exact way something is said, and a translator who tries to keep the meaning usually loses the timing. Romcoms sit somewhere in the middle, which is why studios keep remaking them locally instead of exporting them.

E  Then there is the slow route. The Shawshank Redemption failed at the box office when it was originally released in 1994. It has since become a modern classic, largely because television kept showing it and audiences kept recommending it to each other. Its story — friendship, patience and hope inside a prison — needs no local knowledge at all. Some films do not travel in space so much as in time.

F  None of this means a film must be simple. Audiences are perfectly willing to work; what they are not willing to do is work without a reason. A film that gives them a character worth following will hold them for two hours in any language. A film that does not will be switched off in ten minutes, however stunning the photography is.
